newsitem.title: USA: US senator--try tobacco levy to pay for ID checks.
newsitem.headline: US senator--try tobacco levy to pay for ID checks.

text.p: Senator Tom Harkin said Thursday he would try on the Senate floor to put a 1.1 percent assessment on raw tobacco sales and imports to offset the cost of ID checks on youthful cigarette buyers.

Harkin tried to add the provision to the fiscal 1998 agriculture appropriations bill but was deterred by the reluctance expressed by other members of the Appropriations Committee, which approved the overall $50.5 billion bill and sent it to the floor.

"If you think it's better to take it to the floor, I will," Harkin, Iowa Democrat, said after doubts were raised by panel chairman Ted Stevens, Alaska Republican, and its Democratic leader, Robert Byrd of West Virginia.
"I just didn't anticipate this would be so controversial."

At the subcommittee level, senators decided, because of budgetary constraints, not to provide funds for grants to states to enforce the 18-year-old rule on cigarette sales. The ID checks would be part of Food and Drug Administration regulation of tobacco.
Harkin wanted to piggyback the assessment onto a levy already imposed on sales of raw tobacco and imports to defray the federal deficit.
"The amendment sounds good," said Byrd, who foresaw possible questions if the plan violated the committee's jurisdiction. "Couldn't you wait until the floor? I might be able to vote for it."

Stevens said he was reluctant to act without knowing the outcome of a proposed agreement between states and cigarette makers over tobacco regulation. The ID checks might become part of that deal, he said.
